unresolvedReferences.description: Fang Yingshu and Wang Shaozong appear without date-bearing wording; recorded as undated attestations.
The Pu clan magnate is unnamed beyond his surname.
Bi Xu's career has no date-bearing wording; recorded as undated.
The translation reads 炕生 as a son named Sheng; the Chinese may instead mean 'Kang's son'. Kept as Sheng per the draft translation.
Li Bao is dated only to the Later (Northern) Wei, 386–534.
The translation renders 魏遊肇 as 'Wei Youzhao'; it means You Zhao of the (Northern) Wei. You Zhao is dated by his own career, 452–520.
Wang Liang, Yu Fu, Emperor Wu of Han, Zhao Pingjun and the Former Emperor are BCE allusions left unresolved.
Prince Xiang's identity is not certain (probably Li Chongmao); left unresolved.
'十三年' is read as Kaiyuan 13 (725), carried over from Kaiyuan 10 in the previous unit.
Xi Jin has no date-bearing wording; recorded as undated.
Mei Fu is a BCE allusion left unresolved.
Li Jiao's meeting with the fourteen-year-old Qi Huan has no date basis; undated.
Chen Xilie, Song Yao, Miao Jinqing and Wei Shu are praised without a date; undated.
Wei Sheng's wife is named only by the surname Zheng.
